cards.title: Notch calculator module: RATING_SCALE, notchChange, notchCalculator (REQ-06-02)
cards.context:
WHY: REQ-06-02 needs a pure, synchronous notch calculator. Other POC parts import it, and Indicator 12 (card T-02) builds on its notchChange. Project rules (CLAUDE.md): plain Node 18+ ESM (.mjs), no npm dependencies, pure functions with no I/O in src/ratings, tests use node:test + node:assert/strict. Do not use APIs newer than Node 18 (no toSorted, no Object.groupBy).

FILES: create src/ratings/notch.mjs and test/ratings/notch.test.mjs. Keep src/.gitkeep and test/.gitkeep as they are; deleting them is optional.

CONTRACT (exact names; the module exports exactly these three and nothing else):
- export const RATING_SCALE = Object.freeze(["AAA","AA+","AA","AA-","A+","A","A-","BBB+","BBB","BBB-","BB+","BB","BB-","B+","B","B-","CCC+","CCC","CCC-"]). 19 ratings, best first, index AAA=0 ... CCC-=18. Must be frozen.
- export function notchChange(previous, current) -> integer = index(current) - index(previous). Positive = downgrade, negative = upgrade, range -18..18. Unchanged must return +0, not -0 (Object.is(result, 0)).
- export function notchCalculator(previous, current) -> { notches, direction, wl } with exactly these three keys. notches = notchChange(previous, current). direction is "downgrade" if n>0, "upgrade" if n<0, "unchanged" if n===0. wl uses the Ind. 13 thresholds: 0 if n<=1 (upgrades, unchanged and a 1-notch downgrade), 1 if n===2, 2 if n>=3.
- All functions are synchronous and return plain values, never Promises. No console output and no imports of node:fs, node:http, node:net, node:child_process or any other I/O module.

INPUT VALIDATION (C1), shared by both functions, in one internal non-exported helper:
1. If typeof value !== 'string', throw RangeError. This check comes BEFORE .trim(), so null, undefined, 7, {}, [] and new String('AAA') give RangeError, not TypeError.
2. Compute value.trim().toUpperCase(), look it up in RATING_SCALE. Not found -> RangeError.
3. The RangeError message names the argument ('previous' or 'current') and the bad value. Message text is not part of the contract; tests assert the type only.
ASCII hyphen-minus only: U+2212 and the en dash are rejected. Inner whitespace is not stripped ('BBB +' and 'B B' throw).

BINDING DECISION (C2): the POC text example 'BBB+ -> BB+ = 2 notches -> WL 1' is WRONG. Correct: 3 notches / WL 2. Do not 'fix' this back. The calculator thresholds (>=2 -> 1, >=3 -> 2) are deliberately different from Indicator 12's (card T-02). Do not share threshold code between the two.

UNIT TESTS (test/ratings/notch.test.mjs): cover every acceptance item below, including the full 361-pair loop (19x19) and every invalid input of AC-4, each as previous and as current. Test frozen behaviour inside the ES module (strict mode): push and index assignment throw TypeError, array unchanged afterwards.

OUT OF SCOPE: Indicator 13 as its own export, ratings outside the 19-step scale, outlook suffixes, override/persistence/logging, any change to package.json.
acceptance: AC-1: Given `src/ratings/notch.mjs`, when `RATING_SCALE` is imported, then it deep-strict-equals `["AAA","AA+","AA","AA-","A+","A","A-","BBB+","BBB","BBB-","BB+","BB","BB-","B+","B","B-","CCC+","CCC","CCC-"]`, its `length === 19` and `Object.isFrozen(RATING_SCALE) === true`.

AC-1: Given the frozen `RATING_SCALE` in an ES module (strict mode), when the test calls `RATING_SCALE.push("D")` or assigns `RATING_SCALE[0] = "X"`, then each throws `TypeError`, and afterwards the array still deep-equals the 19-item list with length 19.

AC-2: Given valid ratings, when `notchChange(previous, current)` is called, then it returns `index(current) − index(previous)`: `("BBB+","BB+") → 3`, `("BBB+","BBB-") → 2`, `("BBB+","BBB") → 1`, `("BB+","BBB+") → -3`, `("AAA","CCC-") → 18`, `("CCC-","AAA") → -18`.
AC-2: Given the same rating twice, when `notchChange("A","A")` is called, then `Object.is(result, 0) === true` (positive zero, not `-0`).
AC-2: Given all 361 pairs from `RATING_SCALE` × `RATING_SCALE`, when `notchChange(p, c)` is called, then `Number.isInteger(result)` is true and `-18 <= result <= 18`.

AC-3, C1, X-trim: Given input that differs from a scale rating only by case or by leading/trailing whitespace (as removed by `String.prototype.trim()`), when `notchChange` is called, then it uses that rating: `("bbb+","BB+") === 3`, `("  BBB+ ","\tbb+\n") === 3`, `(" aa-","AA- ") === 0`, `(" aa-","AA- ") === 0`.
AC-3: Given mixed case and whitespace, when `notchCalculator(" bBb+","bbb- ")` is called, then the result deep-strict-equals `{ notches: 2, direction: "downgrade", wl: 1 }`.

AC-4, C1: Given each invalid value from the list `""`, `"   "`, `"BBB++"`, `"D"`, `"NR"`, `"Baa1"`, `"AAA+"`, `"CCC--"`, `"BBB +"`, `"B B"`, `null`, `undefined`, `7`, `{}`, `[]`, when it is passed as `previous` (with `current = "AAA"`) and then as `current` (with `previous = "AAA"`), then `notchChange` throws `RangeError` and does not throw `TypeError` (`assert.throws(fn, RangeError)`). The test covers 15 values × 2 positions.
AC-4: Given the same 15 invalid values in both positions, when `notchCalculator` is called, then it throws `RangeError` and does not throw `TypeError`. The test covers 15 values × 2 positions.

AC-5, C2: Given `("BBB+","BB+")`, when `notchCalculator` is called, then the result deep-strict-equals `{ notches: 3, direction: "downgrade", wl: 2 }` and `Object.keys(result).sort()` deep-equals `["direction","notches","wl"]` (no extra keys).
AC-5, C2: Given `("BBB+","BBB-")`, when `notchCalculator` is called, then the result deep-strict-equals `{ notches: 2, direction: "downgrade", wl: 1 }`.

AC-6, C6: Given downgrades at each threshold, when `notchCalculator` is called, then it returns `("BBB+","BBB") → { notches: 1, direction: "downgrade", wl: 0 }`, `("A","BBB+") → { notches: 2, direction: "downgrade", wl: 1 }`, `("A","BBB") → { notches: 3, direction: "downgrade", wl: 2 }` and `("AAA","CCC-") → { notches: 18, direction: "downgrade", wl: 2 }`.

AC-7, C3, C5: Given upgrades, when `notchCalculator` is called, then it returns `("BBB","BBB+") → { notches: -1, direction: "upgrade", wl: 0 }`, `("BB+","BBB+") → { notches: -3, direction: "upgrade", wl: 0 }` and `("CCC-","AAA") → { notches: -18, direction: "upgrade", wl: 0 }`.

AC-8, C3: Given the same rating twice, in any case or whitespace, when `notchCalculator` is called with `("A","a ")`, `("AAA","AAA")` or `("CCC-","CCC-")`, then each result deep-strict-equals `{ notches: 0, direction: "unchanged", wl: 0 }`. `notches` must be `+0`, because `deepStrictEqual` rejects `-0`.

AC-9, C5: Given all 361 pairs `(p, c)` from `RATING_SCALE`, with `n = notchChange(p, c)`, when `notchCalculator(p, c)` is called, then `notches === n`. `direction` is `"downgrade"` if n>0, `"upgrade"` if n<0 and `"unchanged"` if n===0. `wl` is 0 if n<=1, 1 if n===2 and 2 if n>=3.

AC-13: Given `await import("../../src/ratings/notch.mjs")`, when its keys are listed, then `Object.keys(mod).sort()` deep-equals `["RATING_SCALE","notchCalculator","notchChange"]` and there is no default export.

AC-13, C8: Given valid inputs, when `notchChange("BBB+","BB+")` and `notchCalculator("BBB+","BB+")` are called, then neither result is a `Promise` (`!(r instanceof Promise)` and `typeof r?.then !== "function"`).

AC-13, C8: Given `mock.method(console, "log" | "error" | "warn")`, when both functions are called with valid input and also with invalid input (where the throw is caught), then each mock has `callCount() === 0`.

AC-13, CLAUDE.md: Given the source text of `src/ratings/notch.mjs`, when its import statements are inspected, then it has no imports at all. In particular it does not import `node:fs`, `fs`, `node:http`, `node:https`, `node:net`, `node:child_process`, `node:process` or another I/O module.

notes.note: gate failed only because verify 'node --test test/ratings/' (directory form) errors MODULE_NOT_FOUND on Node 22; dev's 27 tests pass on Node 20 and by file/glob form

cards.title: Indicator 12 country rating change WL: countryRatingChangeWl (REQ-03-12)
cards.context:
WHY: REQ-03-12 (Indicator 12) needs the Watchlist level (WL, 0-4 scale, higher is worse) for a change in the client's country rating. This function returns only 0, 1 or 2. It is built on notchChange from card T-01, which must be merged first.

Project rules (CLAUDE.md): plain Node 18+ ESM (.mjs), no npm dependencies, pure functions with no I/O in src/indicators, tests use node:test + node:assert/strict.

FILES: create src/indicators/countryRating.mjs and test/indicators/countryRating.test.mjs. Do NOT modify src/ratings/notch.mjs, which is owned by T-01.

CONTRACT:
- import { notchChange } from '../ratings/notch.mjs' (this exact relative path).
- export function countryRatingChangeWl(previous, current) -> 0 | 1 | 2. Let n = notchChange(previous, current). Return 0 if n<=0 (upgrade or unchanged), 1 if n===1, 2 if n>=2. This is the module's only export.
- Validation comes from notchChange: input is trimmed with String.prototype.trim() and case-insensitive; a non-string or unknown rating throws RangeError (not TypeError). Do not catch or rewrap the error. Do not add a second validation path.
- Synchronous (no Promise). No console output, no I/O imports. No state between calls: no caching, no module-level mutable variables, no override parameter (C7: 'editable' is met by calling again with the edited value).

BINDING DECISION (C6): Indicator 12 thresholds are deliberately different from the calculator's Ind. 13 thresholds. A 1-notch downgrade gives Ind. 12 WL 1 but notchCalculator wl 0. Do not reuse notchCalculator().wl.

UNIT TESTS (test/indicators/countryRating.test.mjs): cover every acceptance item below, including the 361-pair loop over RATING_SCALE (import from ../../src/ratings/notch.mjs), the invalid inputs of AC-4 (each as previous and as current), and a check that package.json has no dependencies or devDependencies (read it with node:fs in the TEST only; the src file must not import fs).

OUT OF SCOPE: fetching/pre-filling the country rating from a public source (C4), persistence, audit, UI and printed output (C8), any change to package.json.
acceptance: AC-3, C1, X-trim: Given input that differs from a scale rating only by case or by leading/trailing whitespace, when `countryRatingChangeWl` is called, then it uses that rating: `("ccc","CCC-") === 1`, `(" bbb+ ","\tbbb\n") === 1`, `(" aa","a- ") === 2`.

AC-4, C1: Given each invalid value from the list `""`, `"   "`, `"BBB++"`, `"D"`, `"NR"`, `"Baa1"`, `"AAA+"`, `"CCC--"`, `"BBB +"`, `"B B"`, `null`, `undefined`, `7`, `{}`, `[]`, when it is passed as `previous` (with `current = "AAA"`) and then as `current` (with `previous = "AAA"`), then `countryRatingChangeWl` throws `RangeError` and does not throw `TypeError`. The test covers 15 values × 2 positions, and the error comes from `notchChange` unchanged (not caught or wrapped).

AC-10, REQ-03-12: Given downgrades, when `countryRatingChangeWl` is called, then it returns `("BBB+","BBB") → 1`, `("BBB+","BBB-") → 2`, `("BBB+","BB+") → 2`, `("AAA","CCC-") → 2`, `("CCC","CCC-") → 1` and `("AAA","AA+") → 1`.
AC-11, C3: Given an upgrade or no change, when `countryRatingChangeWl` is called with `("BBB","BBB+")`, `("CCC-","AAA")` or `("A","A")`, then each returns `0` (strictly `=== 0`).

AC-10, AC-11, C6: Given all 361 pairs `(p, c)` from `RATING_SCALE` (imported from `../../src/ratings/notch.mjs`), with `n = notchChange(p, c)`, when `countryRatingChangeWl(p, c)` is called, then the result is in `[0, 1, 2]` and equals 0 if n<=0, 1 if n===1 and 2 if n>=2.

AC-11, C6: Given the 1-notch downgrade `("BBB+","BBB")`, when both functions are called, then `countryRatingChangeWl("BBB+","BBB") === 1` while `notchCalculator("BBB+","BBB").wl === 0`. The two threshold sets are different.

AC-12, C7: Given these calls in sequence, then the results are: `countryRatingChangeWl("AA","A-") === 2`, then `countryRatingChangeWl("AA","AA-") === 1` (the edited current value), then `countryRatingChangeWl("AA","A-") === 2` again.

AC-12, C7: Given the function signature, when it is inspected, then `countryRatingChangeWl.length === 2` and it takes no override parameter. Calling with a third extra argument, `("AA","A-","AA-")`, still returns `2`.
AC-13: Given `await import("../../src/indicators/countryRating.mjs")`, when its keys are listed, then `Object.keys(mod)` deep-equals `["countryRatingChangeWl"]` and there is no default export.

AC-13: Given the source text of `src/indicators/countryRating.mjs`, when its imports are inspected, then the only import is `import { notchChange } from "../ratings/notch.mjs"` (that relative path, single or double quotes). There is no import of `node:fs`, `fs`, `node:http`, `node:https`, `node:net`, `node:child_process` or another I/O module.

AC-13, C8: Given valid input, when `countryRatingChangeWl("BBB+","BB+")` is called, then the result is not a `Promise` (`!(r instanceof Promise)` and `typeof r?.then !== "function"`) and it is `=== 2`.

AC-13, C8: Given `mock.method(console, "log" | "error" | "warn")`, when the function is called with valid input and also with invalid input (where the throw is caught), then each mock has `callCount() === 0`.
AC-14: Given the repository `package.json`, read with `node:fs` in the test file only, when it is parsed, then it has no `dependencies` key and no `devDependencies` key (both `undefined`).

AC-14, DEL-ci: Given the integration worktree with T-01 and T-02 merged, when `node --test` runs at its root, then it exits with code 0 and its output includes tests from both `test/ratings/notch.test.mjs` and `test/indicators/countryRating.test.mjs`. The card's own verify step is `node --test test/indicators/`, so this full-suite check is run at integration.

cards.context:
PREVIOUS WORK EXISTS: card T-01 (blocked only because its verify command failed on Node 22) produced a passing implementation in commit 8b71c33 on branch job/JOB-20261004-1255-rating-notch-calculator-and-coun--T-01. FIRST run `git cherry-pick 8b71c33` in your worktree, review it against the spec, fix anything wrong, and re-run verify. Do not rewrite from scratch unless the cherry-pick is unusable.

WHY: REQ-06-02 needs a pure, synchronous notch calculator. Other POC parts import it, and Indicator 12 (card T-02) builds on its notchChange. Project rules (CLAUDE.md): plain Node 18+ ESM (.mjs), no npm dependencies, pure functions with no I/O in src/ratings, tests use node:test + node:assert/strict. No APIs newer than Node 18.

FILES: src/ratings/notch.mjs and test/ratings/notch.test.mjs.

CONTRACT (module exports exactly these three): RATING_SCALE = Object.freeze of the 19 ratings AAA..CCC- (best first, index AAA=0 ... CCC-=18); notchChange(previous, current) -> integer index(current)-index(previous), +0 when unchanged; notchCalculator(previous, current) -> { notches, direction, wl } exactly these keys, direction downgrade/upgrade/unchanged by sign, wl 0 if n<=1, 1 if n===2, 2 if n>=3 (Ind. 13 thresholds). Synchronous, no console output, no I/O imports.

INPUT VALIDATION (C1): internal non-exported helper; typeof value !== 'string' -> RangeError BEFORE .trim(); then value.trim().toUpperCase() looked up in RATING_SCALE, else RangeError naming the argument and value. ASCII hyphen only; inner whitespace not stripped.

BINDING DECISION (C2): BBB+ -> BB+ is 3 notches / WL 2 (the POC text saying 2 / WL 1 is wrong). Do not share threshold code with Indicator 12.

UNIT TESTS: cover every acceptance item including the 361-pair loop and every invalid input of AC-4 as previous and as current.

OUT OF SCOPE: Indicator 13 as an export, ratings outside the scale, override/persistence/logging, any change to package.json.
acceptance: AC-1: RATING_SCALE deep-equals the 19-item list AAA..CCC-, is frozen, push and index assignment throw TypeError and leave it unchanged
AC-2: notchChange returns index(current) − index(previous) as an integer in -18..18; A→A is +0 (Object.is)
AC-3: input differing only by case or leading/trailing whitespace (incl. NBSP) is accepted; notchCalculator(' bBb+','bbb- ') deep-equals { notches: 2, direction: 'downgrade', wl: 1 }

AC-4: the 15 invalid values ('', '   ', 'BBB++', 'D', 'NR', 'Baa1', 'AAA+', 'CCC--', 'BBB +', 'B B', null, undefined, 7, {}, []) as previous or as current make notchChange and notchCalculator throw RangeError, not TypeError
AC-5: notchCalculator('BBB+','BB+') deep-strict-equals { notches: 3, direction: 'downgrade', wl: 2 } with no extra keys; ('BBB+','BBB-') gives { notches: 2, direction: 'downgrade', wl: 1 }
AC-6: BBB+→BBB = {1,'downgrade',0}; A→BBB+ = {2,'downgrade',1}; A→BBB = {3,'downgrade',2}; AAA→CCC- = {18,'downgrade',2}
AC-7: BBB→BBB+ = {-1,'upgrade',0}; BB+→BBB+ = {-3,'upgrade',0}; CCC-→AAA = {-18,'upgrade',0}
AC-8: ('A','a '), ('AAA','AAA'), ('CCC-','CCC-') → { notches: 0, direction: 'unchanged', wl: 0 }
AC-9: for all 361 pairs notches === notchChange, direction by sign, wl 0 if n<=1, 1 if n===2, 2 if n>=3
AC-13: notch.mjs exports exactly RATING_SCALE, notchChange, notchCalculator; results are not Promises; no imports at all; console.log/error/warn never called
